root_cause.text: The `mangle_content_len` function in `net/netfilter/nf_nat_sip.c` allocates an insufficiently sized stack buffer of 6 bytes (`sizeof("65536")`) to hold the formatted content length string, leading to a stack out-of-bounds write when `sprintf` formats a value larger than 65535.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that the stack buffer size in `mangle_content_len` was increased from `sizeof("65536")` to `sizeof("4294967295")` and `sprintf(buffer, "%u", c_len)` was replaced with `scnprintf` to prevent the stack-out-of-bounds write reported in the KASAN trace.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function allocates a stack buffer of only 6 bytes on line 156: `char buffer[sizeof("65536")];`. It then formats the integer `c_len` into this buffer using `sprintf` on line 171: `buflen = sprintf(buffer, "%u", c_len);`. If `c_len` is negative (which formats to a large unsigned integer of up to 10 digits) or exceeds 99999, the resulting string will exceed the 6-byte buffer, leading to a stack out-of-bounds write.
